name: end of life decisions overview
title: End of life: a patient who cannot decide gets a substitute decision maker in a fixed order; palliative care is reached by four routes and aims at comfort; a patient who asks for medical assistance in dying must meet every eligibility criterion, and the stream (natural death foreseeable or not) sets the safeguards; palliative pearls, MAiD in practice and conscientious objection are below

nodes.title: End of life: who decides, and what can be offered?
lines: capacity (Health Care Consent Act s. 4) = able to UNDERSTAND the information + APPRECIATE the foreseeable consequences of deciding or not · specific to each decision · can fluctuate
code status (which resuscitation, if any) needs informed consent from the patient or SDM · it is NOT the same as goals of care
goals of care: who the patient is, how their values shape their goals, how these fit the clinical picture · prepares for consent decisions
family-centred: dignity and respect for patient, family, significant others throughout

nodes.title: Patient asks for medical assistance in dying (MAiD)
lines: legal in Canada June 2016 · 2 streams since March 2021

nodes.title: Eligible? ALL of these
lines: • eligible for publicly funded health care
• grievous and irremediable: serious illness, advanced irreversible decline, unbearable suffering not relievable in ways they accept
• informed consent: diagnosis, treatments, ways to relieve suffering including palliative care

nodes.title: Substitute decision maker (SDM)
lines: gives or refuses consent for the patient
hierarchy: Health Care Consent Act s. 20

nodes.title: Palliative care
lines: quality of life: physical, psychosocial, spiritual · patient AND family

nodes.title: Any ONE route in
lines: • treatment futile or would cause suffering

nodes.title: Written request
lines: signed before an independent witness (another person may sign if the patient cannot)

nodes.title: Two scales
lines: • Palliative Performance Scale: disease burden, progress to end of life
• Edmonton Symptom Assessment System: symptoms to manage

nodes.title: 2 independent assessors
lines: ONE has expertise in the condition and has discussed all treatment options

nodes.title: Ask the SDM, in this ORDER
lines: 5 · child (16+), custodial parent or Children's Aid Society

nodes.title: Advance care planning
lines: WISHES that guide the SDM, NOT advance consent
~speculation about a future illness, but prepares both

nodes.title: Comfort, at home where possible
lines: • stroke, disability unacceptable to them: no tube feeds or IV fluids
• turning and symptom drugs do NOT hasten death

nodes.title: Consent AGAIN at the time of MAiD
lines: unless a WAIVER of final consent was signed (at risk of losing capacity)

nodes.title: 90-day wait · NO waiver
lines: consent AGAIN at the time of MAiD

panels.title: Palliative pearls and myths
items: UNCERTAINTY: outcomes fall along a spectrum · families may be angry when the patient does better
TEMPORARY improvement for hours to days after stopping feeds or fluids: reassure · re-evaluate if it lasts days
moral distress: 'it's not my journey' · trust the SDM
NOT starving: organs shut down, no hunger or thirst · sips for comfort
turning every 4 hours = comfort + exam · MOTTLING → call the family
patients often die as they lived · let family step away, rest

panels.title: MAiD in practice
items: regional coordination service · home, long-term care or hospital
IV: benzodiazepine → high-dose propofol → neuromuscular blocker · 10 min infusion, death within 10 more
oral lethal drug: an option, rarely used

panels.title: Conscientious objection (CPSO)
items: no physician has to provide MAiD
respect dignity · do NOT impede access
tell the patient directly: a personal, not clinical, reason
